text: Every Friday, pupils at Green Hill School hear familiar voices during the
morning break. The voices come from a small room next to the library, where
a group of pupils makes a radio programme. The programme includes school
news, short interviews and music. It began when an English teacher noticed
that some quiet pupils had interesting ideas but rarely shared them in class.
She wanted to give them another way to be heard.
At first, only six pupils joined the radio team. They used an old computer and
a microphone that the school already owned. Before their first programme,
they asked classmates what they wanted to hear. Most asked for music, but
some wanted advice about school life. The team decided to include both.
Pupils who did not want to speak could choose music or write questions for
interviews. Everyone had a useful job.
Making a programme was harder than the team expected. During their first
interview, two pupils spoke at the same time, so listeners could not
understand the guest's answer. After that, the team began practising
interviews before recording them. They also learnt to ask short questions and
wait for the answers. Now a teacher checks each programme before it is
played. However, the pupils still choose the topics themselves.
After three months, more pupils wanted to join the team. One of them was
Maya, who had been afraid to speak in front of her class. She started by
writing the news and later agreed to read it with a friend. She still feels
nervous before a programme, but she no longer avoids speaking. The team
now hopes to interview people from outside the school. Before doing that, the
pupils need to learn how to arrange interviews with busy guests.
